The Bindal language region included the area from [[Cape Cleveland, Queensland|Cape Cleveland]] extending south towards [[Ayr, Queensland|Ayr]] and the mouth of the [[Burdekin River]], encompassing the landscape within the boundaries of the [[City of Townsville|Townsville City Council]] and [[Shire of Burdekin|Burdekin Shire Council]].{{SLQ-CC-BY|url=https://maps.slq.qld.gov.au/iyil/view/47?embed=true|title=Bindal|author(s)=[[State Library of Queensland]]|accessdate=17 May 2022}} == Classification == Bowern suggests that it might have been a [[Maric language]].Bowern, Claire. 2011. "[http://anggarrgoon.wordpress.com/2011/12/23/how-many-languages-were-spoken-in-australia/ How Many Languages Were Spoken in Australia?]", ''Anggarrgoon: Australian languages on the web'', 23 December 2011 ([http://pamanyungan.sites.yale.edu/master-list-australian-languages-v12 corrected] 6 February 2012) Breen presumes that one of two [[Lower Burdekin languages]], which he concluded were not Maric, is Bindal. == Vocabulary == Some words from the Bindal language, as spelt and written by Bindal authors include: * ''Adha'': yes * ''Andha'': saltwater * ''Bagaraga'': star * ''Barri'': stone * ''Bugan'': grass * ''Gadhara'': possum * ''Gamu'': water * ''Gunbana'': blood == See also == * [[Bindal people]] ==References== {{Reflist}} == External links == * [http://aiatsis.gov.au/sites/default/files/docs/collections/language_bibs/bindal.pdf Bibliography of Bindal people and language resources], at the [[Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies]] {{Use dmy dates|date=June 2019}} {{Pama-Nyungan languages}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Maric languages]] [[Category:Extinct languages of Queensland]] [[Category:Pama–Nyungan languages]] {{ia-lang-stub}}
